speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; to help me determine the cause, please describe when these episodes started and how long they last. Are you experiencing any associated symptoms like hearing loss, tinnitus, nausea, or vision changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. The fact that your dizziness is triggered by changes in position is very specific; does this happen when you roll over in bed, look up, or tilt your head back? Additionally, do you feel any nystagmus (rhythmic eye movements) or have you noticed any new neurological symptoms like numbness or weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The description of sudden, position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old without other neurological deficits is classic for BPPV. Since I have established the clinical suspicion, do you consent to me performing the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis and identify the affected canal?
